_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel's now up four straight weeks — another 3.5c to $5.348/gal for the week ending 8/3, still the Hormuz conflict premium building, not fading. Keep pushing that fuel-surcharge line, it's a trend now, not a spike. On the freight side: Southeast reefer keeps softening as GA/FL produce season winds down — that's the second straight cycle of reports showing Northeast-bound rates down 19-29% off peak, so if you're quoting reefer out of Atlanta or Miami right now, don't quote last month's number, ask what today's board looks like before you counter. Dry van, flatbed, and the rest of spot are still unverified trade press this cycle — hold your ask in conversation, don't quote a rate off it.

_sourcing.status: Diesel RE-VERIFIED and advanced again this cycle: fourth consecutive weekly increase, now $5.348/gal for week ending 2026-08-03 (up from $5.313 the prior week), corroborated across three independent outlets. asOf advanced to 2026-08-03 on diesel's account only. Spot/modality/lanes/commodityRates remain carried-forward for a SEVENTH straight cycle — no clean corroboration again this week, though the Southeast reefer easing story corroborated a second consecutive cycle (still not a clean number to put in a numeric field). See refreshBlockers for egress status.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE, confirmed 2026-08-11: $5.348/gal for the week ending 2026-08-03, up 3.5c (some sources say 4c) from the prior confirmed week's $5.313, marking the FOURTH consecutive week of increases. Corroborated across THREE independent outlets, all EIA-sourced with consistent figures: (1) AgriNews 'Fuel gauge for week ending Aug. 3' — national average diesel rose to $5.348, up from $5.313 the prior week, up $1.548 YoY vs $3.800 a year ago; (2) FleetOwner 'Diesel prices rise to $5.35/gal amid Strait of Hormuz tensions' — EIA-released 8/4, up 4c to $5.348, regional breakdown: Rockies +14c to $5.285, Midwest +7c to $5.262, West Coast +6c to $6.130, Gulf Coast +5c to $5.141, East Coast -6c to $5.299; (3) HaulerMath (EIA-weekly aggregator) independently shows $5.35 for the same week. All three agree on the figure (within rounding), the direction, and the driver (continued Iran/Strait of Hormuz tension, not resolved). Ruled out a false-positive contradiction: a FleetOwner headline reading 'diesel...decline for fourth straight week amid easing global tensions' surfaced in search but checked separately and dates to 2026-06-17 (a much earlier Iran de-escalation period, $5.059/gal) — NOT this cycle's data, correctly excluded. Week-ending-8/10 data (today's scheduled EIA release, published same-day 8/11) was NOT yet surfaced by WebSearch at refresh time — carried the most recent CONFIRMED week (8/3) rather than guess at today's number; one GasBuddy citation floated 'diesel fell 5.1c to $5.275' as of 8/10 but that is retail-pump crowdsourced data on a different methodology than EIA's DOE survey and was not treated as a substitute or a contradiction — noted here for transparency, not promoted. No primary eia.gov fetch was possible (still 403, see refreshBlockers) — this is 3-source secondary corroboration, not a primary-source read, consistent with the bar cleared each of the last three cycles.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 snapshot ($3.83/mi). Not verified this cycle — DAT/SONAR WebFetch still blocked (403), and WebSearch again produced mutually contradictory 'current' figures: dry van spot linehaul cited at $2.32/mi 'this week' (minus fuel, as of 8/3, down 2.4% w/w) in one DAT-sourced snippet, vs. a bellwether-states outbound figure of $3.04/mi (also minus fuel) in the same search cycle, vs. the file's carried $3.83/mi all-in figure — three different bases (linehaul-only vs. all-in, national vs. bellwether-state-weighted) that don't reconcile without a primary DAT Trendlines read. Not promoted.
_sourcing.modality: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 modality ranges. Not verified this cycle. Same pattern as spotAllIn: reefer cited at $2.65/mi 'this week' (minus fuel, down 2.6% w/w) in one search, vs. $3.35/mi including fuel 'as of mid-2026' with contract near $3.28 in another, vs. regional reefer spread $2.71-3.57/mi in a third — again a fuel-inclusive/exclusive and timeframe mismatch, not a single reconciled current reading. Directionally sources agree reefer has traded above contract for the first time since 2022 and remains elevated, but no clean current figure to promote. None promoted.
_sourcing.commodityRates: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle. See lanes note below on why Fresh Produce specifically was not marked down despite the reefer-easing story — no clean $/mi replacement figure found, only percentage-off-peak commentary.
_sourcing.lanes: carried-forward, unchanged, for a second straight cycle despite trying again to find a specific-lane replacement number. The Southeast reefer easing story RE-CONFIRMED this cycle (DAT Reefer Report headlines: 'Florida corrects, California surges — the seasonal handoff is here,' 'Every produce region hits adequate as Florida's slide continues,' Georgia now carrying the Southeast tomato/watermelon basket alone under continued Shortage conditions) — directionally consistent with last cycle's 19-29% Northeast-bound decline. A Miami→Atlanta figure of $2.95/mi surfaced (SupplyChainStack, DAT-sourced) but is dated 'last verified July 6, 2026' — five weeks stale and the reverse direction from the file's Atlanta→Miami entry, so not a clean same-lane/current-week replacement. Yakima→Northeast had no fresh figure at all this cycle. Flagging again for next cycle: if DAT Trendlines becomes fetchable, both lanes are the first candidates to reprice down.
_sourcing.blurb: rewritten this cycle: diesel is now four weeks into the climb (not three), Hormuz premium still building not fading, coaching unchanged (push surcharge, don't ease off). Added explicit reefer-quoting caution given the second-cycle-confirmed Southeast easing trend, without putting an unverified number in the blurb.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Seventh straight cycle without clean spot/modality/lanes corroboration. Trade press directionally still says dry van is above contract, flatbed is near record highs, and Southeast reefer is now confirmed (two cycles running) to be softening off its summer peak as produce season transitions from Florida to Georgia. None of that is precise enough to put in numeric fields without a primary source read. Do not promote until dat.com/trendlines or eia.gov is actually reachable.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed: curl to https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/ returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' again today; the agent-proxy status endpoint ($HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status) logged a fresh connect_rejected entry for www.eia.gov:443 at refresh time ('gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)'). Block is unchanged across all seven weekly refreshes from 07-07 through 08-11 — destination-side 403 via the agent proxy, not a proxy outage; DAT.com was not re-tested by direct curl this cycle (same proxy policy applies, WebSearch used instead) since eia.gov's result already answered the egress question. WebSearch works and this cycle it cleanly re-verified diesel's continued climb: three independent outlets (AgriNews, FleetOwner, HaulerMath) agree on $5.348/gal for the week ending 2026-08-03, up 3.5-4c, fourth straight weekly increase, still driven by the Iran/Hormuz conflict — clean enough to promote to LIVE and advance asOf to 2026-08-03. Today's scheduled EIA release (week ending 8/10, published same-day) was not yet surfaced by WebSearch at refresh time, so no guess was made at it; next cycle should check for it first. Spot/modality searches again produced mutually contradictory 'current' figures split across linehaul-only-minus-fuel vs. all-in-with-fuel bases and different reference weeks (see per-field notes) — none promoted, asOf not advanced on their account. Lanes: tried specifically to replace the Atlanta-Miami/Yakima reefer entries per this cycle's brief, found only a stale (7/6), reverse-direction Miami-Atlanta figure — not clean enough to promote (see lanes note). Broader web-fetch access (not just search) to a primary source like eia.gov or dat.com/trendlines would let spot/modality/lanes get the same clean-primary-source treatment diesel has now gotten four cycles running, instead of waiting on secondary-outlet agreement that keeps splitting on methodology (linehaul vs. all-in, weekly vs. monthly).
